question.worked_solution:
The difference formula for cosine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
3\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3\operatorname{sin}⁡x=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
3\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3\operatorname{sin}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=3 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=3\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{1}{1} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =1 \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1) \\ ϕ & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={3}^{2}+(3)^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =2\cdot {3}^{2} \\ {R}^{2} & =18 \\ R & =3\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
3\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3\operatorname{sin}⁡x=3\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-{45}^{∘})
$$

last_observation.worked_solution:
The difference formula for cosine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
3\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3\operatorname{sin}⁡x=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
3\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3\operatorname{sin}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=3 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=3\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{1}{1} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =1 \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1) \\ ϕ & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & ={3}^{2}+(3)^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =2\cdot {3}^{2} \\ {R}^{2} & =18 \\ R & =3\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
3\operatorname{cos}⁡x+3\operatorname{sin}⁡x=3\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-{45}^{∘})
$$

question.problem: Given that the expression $\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$
question.worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-3\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{3} \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=3\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\sqrt{3} \\ ϕ & ={60}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.problem: Given that the expression $2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$
question.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=6\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{6}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =3 \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

3sin⁡x−3cos⁡x=Rsin⁡(x−ϕ),

we get the following identity:

3sin⁡x−3cos⁡x=(Rcos⁡ϕ)sin⁡x−(Rsin⁡ϕ)cos⁡x

Equating the coefficients of sin⁡x and cos⁡x, we get the following system of equations:

{Rcos⁡ϕ=3Rsin⁡ϕ=3

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

Rsin⁡ϕRcos⁡ϕ=33tan⁡ϕ=3ϕ=60∘.

$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=6\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{6}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =3 \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3).\end{aligned}
